title: Kingdom of France

lead.label: Overview
lead.text: France in 1700 was governed under Louis XIV’s personal monarchy. The court and central government were based at Versailles, while royal officers carried the crown’s authority into the provinces.

organization.label: Entity type
organization.text: Kingdom under Louis XIV, King of France and Navarre.

organization.label: Government
organization.text: Personal royal government without a first minister; the king reserved the final decision.
organization.scope: Mature reign of Louis XIV; applies in 1700

organization.label: Institutions
organization.text: Specialized royal councils addressed state affairs, finances, religion and domestic administration. Ministers advised the king.
organization.scope: Mature reign; no day-specific council session claimed

organization.label: Seat / capital
organization.text: Versailles: royal court and center of government; the court had moved there in 1682.

organization.label: Administrative relationships
organization.text: Intendants served as royal officers in the provinces, connecting central authority with provincial administration.

changes.text: After Mazarin’s death, Louis announced that he would govern without a first minister.
The royal court moved to Versailles, consolidating a central setting for government and court life.

population.label: Population
population.text: No population observation is admitted for France at this date. The displayed cross-channel portion is not the whole kingdom.

overview.label: Authority at court
overview.text: Louis XIV’s absolutist claim placed the sovereign at the center of government. His councils and ministers handled distinct areas of business, but the monarch retained the final decision. This short account describes the organization of the reign, rather than every local practice in 1700.

overview.label: Center and provinces
overview.text: The court at Versailles was a political institution as well as a residence. Provincial intendants provided a link with central royal government. The map’s retained regional slice should not be mistaken for a full administrative map of the kingdom.
